title: Automatic Upgrade to Zscaler Admin Console

blocks.text: Zscaler is upgrading organizations to Zscaler Admin Console, a centralized unified platform that provides a more secure and streamlined user experience. Administrators can now access and manage all the Zscaler products, unified policies and security analytics in one place.
Starting September 6, 2026, some organizations are scheduled for an automatic upgrade to Zscaler Admin Console.
This article provides an overview of the upgrade process, upgrade options, and critical changes to the Authentication Service admins' login experience.
Zscaler will send email notifications to your organization's admin accounts about the upgrade schedules.
To ensure a seamless transition, you can choose between a self-managed upgrade or an automatic upgrade:

blocks.item: Self-Managed Upgrade (Recommended): You can choose to upgrade ahead of the scheduled date, to align with your organization’s preferred maintenance window. To begin this process, contact your Zscaler Account team. To learn more, see Migrating Zscaler Service Admins to Authentication Service.
Automatic Upgrade: If no action is taken, Zscaler performs the upgrade automatically on the scheduled date.
Admin access via your organization's external identity provider (IdP) to the legacy service admin portals will be discontinued. Admins must reconfigure their IdPs in Authentication Service.
There will be no impact to end-user authentication and their access to Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA) remains uninterrupted throughout this upgrade.

blocks.text: After the automatic upgrade is completed, the following changes to the login and authentication processes will take effect immediately:

blocks.item: Discontinuation of Legacy IdP Access: Admin access via your organization's external identity provider (IdP) to the legacy service admin portals will be discontinued. Admins will only be directed to Zscaler Admin Console. Admins will be registered as hosted admins on Authentication Service. This can be removed when you reconfigure the IdP.
IdP Reconfiguration: Admins must reconfigure the IdP within the new Authentication Service tenant provisioned for your organization. To learn more, see About External Identity Providers.

Mandatory MFA Enrollment: For enhanced security, all admins are required to enroll in the Zscaler multi-factor authentication (MFA) to gain initial access to Zscaler Admin Console. This is a one-time requirement that must be completed during the initial login after the upgrade. To learn more, see Configuring Multi-Factor Authentication.

API Authentication: If you have Internet & SaaS API authentication configured in the legacy Authentication Service Admin Portal, you must use the same password during the first login, as creating a new password results in loss of access to your legacy APIs. If you do not have Internet & SaaS API authentication, you can create a new password.
Automatic Upgraded IdP and Admin Redirection:

If the IdP is configured in Authentication Service and the admin starts an IdP-initiated login from Authentication Service, the admin is redirected to the IdP (e.g., Okta) for verification. The IdP uses the existing valid session and redirects the admin to MFA.

If the password is already configured in Authentication Service, and the admin starts an IdP-initiated login from the Internet & SaaS or Private Access tile in the IdP, the admin is redirected to the Zscaler Admin Console login page, where the admin can log in using the configured password and then proceed to MFA verification.

If the admin does not have an IdP and password set up in Authentication Service and starts an IdP-initiated login from the Internet & SaaS or Private Access tile in the IdP, the admin is redirected to the Zscaler Admin Console login page, where the admin can either log in using the existing Internet & SaaS or Private Access password or create a new password. If the admin logs in using the Internet & SaaS or Private Access password, that password is migrated to Zscaler Admin Console.
